extracted.intended_audience: philosophers of mathematics, historians of mathematics, mathematicians and graduate students interested in mathematical practice
extracted.subtask_description: An introductory overview and editorial framing for work in the philosophy of mathematical practice, articulating what topics, methods, and standards such work should address and how contributions should be organized (pedagogical introductions paired with research articles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for mathematical practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide philosophical work that is informed by, and seeks to account for, many central aspects of mathematical practice that previous philosophers and logicians have largely ignored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unify efforts of philosophers who attend to practice; the book aims to provide a representative sample of work informed by mathematical practice. Emphasis on paying attention to actual branches of mathematics (geometry, topology, etc.) rather than only abstract foundational problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual pedagogical and research usefulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Make contributions both accessible to a wide audience (undergraduates and non-specialists) and also push research frontiers for specialists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each topic should be discussed in an introductory chapter (general and accessible overview) and a research article (advancing the field). Editorial organization should support both pedagogical aims and first-rate research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide contextual introduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Situate contributions within the broader intellectual and historical context from which they arise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editor(s) should provide an introduction that explains the landscape, motivations, and relations among contributions so readers (including the non-initiated) understand origins and contrasts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extend epistemology beyond 'access' problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Address epistemological issues of mathematics beyond the classic problem of how we have access to abstract objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topics to include: fruitfulness, evidence, visualization, diagrammatic reasoning, understanding, explanation — issues orthogonal to the access problem but central to mathematical epistemology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use detailed case studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ historical and contemporary case studies from specific areas of mathematics to illuminate philosophical problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Like philosophy of natural science, philosophy of mathematics should combine general methodology with revealing case studies (historical and contemporary) drawn from areas such as geometry, knot theory, algebraic topology, cohomology, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain mathematical growth and methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigate how mathematical knowledge grows and what constitutes methodological transitions and change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider models of transitions between mathematical practices (Kitcher): generalization, rigorization, systematization; ask what makes mathematical progress and how discovery relates to justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attention to styles of reasoning and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Study how styles of reasoning evolve, how mathematicians justify programs, and what obstacles and choices shape mathematical research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze reasons mathematicians view domains as worthy, how they steer programs, and the dialectical processes (rational reconstruction vs historical development) affecting methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be informed by history and 'real' mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid analyses that rely only on foundational fragments; instead be informed by the concerns, history, and practice of working mathematicians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corfield's notion of a 'philosophy of real mathematics' draws a line between work grounded in mathematicians' concerns and that based on token contact with history/practice; avoid the 'foundationalist filter.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate concept fruitfulness and naturalness
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain why some mathematical entities and concepts are important, natural, and fruitful while others are not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study criteria that make concepts productive across problems and areas; include historical and structural explanations for fruitfulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for connectivity across mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how and why concepts from one area of mathematics become connected to apparently unrelated areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate mechanisms, historical developments, and explanatory frameworks that produce surprising interconnections in mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess the epistemic role of computer proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze why computer-assisted or computer-generated proofs may fail to provide the sort of understanding mathematicians seek.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish verification from understanding; address limits of computer proofs regarding explanation, insight, and fruitfulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze analogy and inductive reasoning in mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine the role of analogy and other inductive reasoning methods in mathematical practice and whether frameworks like Bayesianism can be applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider forms of inductive support, analogical transfer, and probabilistic reasoning as part of mathematical heuristics and discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relate diagrammatic thinking to formal reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Study the relationship between diagram-based/intuitive reasoning and formal proof-based reasoning, including the fruitfulness of diagrammatic methods in areas such as algebraic topology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address how diagrams contribute to discovery, justification, and communication; ask how to account for their epistemic reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-foundationalism (mathematics as fallible activity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt the view that there is no certain foundation for mathematics and that mathematics is a fallible, practice-driven activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the 'maverick' tradition: accept revisability and fallibility as central methodological features; this influences how progress and justification are conceived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skepticism about logicism's sufficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that mathematical logic alone cannot adequately analyze mathematics and its historical development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complement logical/formal tools with historical, methodological, and practice-sensitive analyses; avoid treating logic as the sole arbiter of philosophical accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine rational reconstruction with historical development
rubrics_metrics.description: Use both idealized rational reconstructions and historical narratives to analyze mathematical episodes (Lakatosian-style dialectic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge the problematic but productive relation between the abstracted, reconstructed account and messy historical development; use both to illuminate methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage foundationalist results where relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: While critical of a purely foundationalist perspective, recognize that foundational research (e.g., reverse mathematics, proof theory, intuitionism) can illuminate aspects of practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Situate foundational insights in dialogue with practice-sensitive questions rather than dismissing them outright.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make philosophy relevant to practicing mathematicians
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim for philosophical work that matters to mathematicians and reflects their concerns rather than being isolated on abstract ontological issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid producing work 'dead to what mathematicians think'; strive for topics and analysis that mathematicians recognize as addressing real mathematical problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use interdisciplinary analogies and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Borrow methodological approaches from philosophy of natural science—combine general methodology with case studies and historical analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt the mixed strategy of methodology + detailed case studies (both historical and contemporary) used in philosophy of the sciences to yield revealing analyses in mathematics.
